commits.author: Khalid Hindawi
commits.subject: fix(cli): error boundary so action failures don't crash the process (#728)
commits.body:
src/cli/index.ts ended with a sync `program.parse()` and no catch, so any
Error thrown by an action handler (e.g. "Task <id> not found" from
complete-task / update-task) escaped as an uncaught exception — crashing with
a full JS stack trace + "Node.js vX" footer (louder on Node v25) and leaving
task status transitions looking "stuck" on the dashboard.

Switch to `program.parseAsync(process.argv).catch()` → clean one-line stderr +
exit(1). commander v14 awaits action results, so sync throws surface here as
rejections. Covers all subcommands incl. bus complete-task/update-task.

Adds tests/integration/cli-error-boundary.test.ts (spawns the source via tsx,
no build step needed): unknown-id complete-task/update-task -> exit 1, clean
message, no stack/crash footer.

Co-authored-by: devops-agent <devops@jmtf.local>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: WillTaylor3698
commits.subject: fix(security): sanitize display-name in formatTelegramReaction — close the #606 residual (last unhardened formatTelegram* path) (#708)
commits.body:
Sentinel finding (AUDIT-upstream-security-delta-2026-07-02.md), toolsmith-
confirmed firsthand: the reaction header interpolated ${from} raw while all
5 sibling formatTelegram* paths wrap sanitizeForPtyInjection. The caller's
stripControlChars deliberately keeps \n/\r (validate.ts char class), so a
display-name carrying a newline + forged '=== TELEGRAM ... ===' /
'Reply using: cortextos bus' line passed unquoted into the agent PTY
(#592/#597 display-name header-forgery class). Real-world severity LOW for
this fleet (ALLOWED_USER id-gate) — defense-in-depth + sibling consistency.

Fix at the formatter boundary, matching the siblings. Two regression tests:
\n-forgery neutralized ([quoted] prefix, no line-anchored header), bare-CR
forgery folded to LF and quoted. Mutation-witnessed: both tests FAIL with
the sanitize removed (66/66 with it).

Co-authored-by: William Taylor <william.taylor@neutralis.it>
Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(templates): quote date -u format so agent records get stamped (#885)
commits.body:
Agent templates instruct agents to stamp memory and heartbeat records with
`date -u +%H:%M UTC` and `date -u +%H:%M:%S UTC`. The bare `UTC` token after
the format string is parsed as a positional operand, so `date` rejects it,
exits 1 and prints nothing -- while the wrapping `echo`/heredoc still exits 0.

    $ echo "NOTE $(date -u +%H:%M UTC): decision"
    NOTE : decision                    <- echo exit 0

The result is a well-formed record with an empty timestamp, written
successfully, with no error surfaced anywhere. Every agent scaffolded from
these templates has been writing unstamped entries; the only signal is a
missing timestamp inside an otherwise correct-looking record.

Quote the format string so it is a single operand:

    $ date -u +'%H:%M UTC'
    21:50 UTC                          (exit 0)

62 occurrences across 26 files: 36 in templates/ (14 files) and 26 in
community/ (12 files). community/ is included rather than deferred because it
is the same defect and those are the agents a catalog install actually
creates.

Deliberately unchanged: `date -u +%H:%M` in templates/hermes/HEARTBEAT.md and
the 8 `date -u +%H:%M:%S)` occurrences in orchestrator and community skills --
those formats are terminated correctly and already work.

Quotes are placed after the `+` to match existing repo convention: `date +'...'`
already appears 26 times in templates/, several on the line directly above a
fixed occurrence. The `"+..."` form appears nowhere in the repo.

Co-authored-by: Boris <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Aaron Sachs
commits.subject: feat(slack): add Socket Mode adapter for per-agent messaging (#906)
commits.body:
* feat(slack): add Socket Mode adapter for per-agent messaging

Agents can now be messaged over Slack in addition to Telegram. One shared
Socket Mode WebSocket connection per org (Slack apps are per-workspace,
n...[truncated]

* fix(slack): keep node engines floor at >=20

asachs01's PR raised the framework-wide engines floor to node >=22 for the
Slack Socket Mode inbound feature, which relies on Node 22's native WebSocket
global. The adapter already self-degrades to "Slack inactive" on runtimes that
predate that global, so the inbound feature does not require raising the floor
for the entire framework. Keep the baseline at >=20 so node-20 users retain the
adapter (inbound auto-disabled below node 22, outbound unaffected).

Co-Authored-By: Aaron Sachs <898627+asachs01@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

commits.body:
* feat(buzz): add Nostr/NIP-29 relay adapter for per-agent messaging

Agents can now be messaged over a Buzz (Nostr NIP-29 group chat) relay,
alongside Telegram. Direct WebSocket + NIP-29 client (no ACP subprocess) so
agents stay on the existing ClaudePTY runtime.

- src/buzz/event.ts: NIP-01 event construction + BIP-340 schnorr signing
  (@noble/secp256k1 + @noble/hashes — one deliberate exception to the
  zero-runtime-deps convention, see PR description for reasoning).
- src/buzz/relay-client.ts: connect -> NIP-42 AUTH challenge/response ->
  subscribe/publish, epoch-guarded reconnect with backoff, EOSE-gated
  message delivery (historical backlog never replays to handlers).
- src/buzz/identity.ts: buzz.json + BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY loading, fail-closed
  allowed_pubkeys allowlist (empty = deny all).
- src/buzz/dispatcher.ts: N:1 channel fan-out — a channel message can reach
  multiple agents, unlike Telegram's 1:1 bot relationship.
- CLI: cortextos buzz send/test-send/discover-channels.
- bus/send-buzz.sh entry point for the injected "Reply using:" line.
- Daemon wiring: queueBuzzMessage/formatBuzzTextMessage in fast-checker.ts
  (parallel queue to Telegram's), org-level singleton relay client in
  agent-manager.ts (started once by the orchestrator, every agent in the
  org registers into the shared dispatcher). Non-blocking by construction
  — a Buzz outage or bad config can never block agent/orchestrator startup.
- add-agent.ts: --buzz-channel flag scaffolds buzz.json. Deliberately does
  NOT auto-generate a keypair — identity minting stays a separate,
  out-of-band operator step (buzz-admin generate-key), matching Slack's
  precedent of requiring manual app/token setup.
- engines.node bumped >=20 -> >=22 (native WebSocket, same floor Slack's
  Socket Mode needs).
- docs/runbook/buzz-adapter-setup.md, templates/{agent,orchestrator,
  analyst}/CLAUDE.md updated per the Agent Awareness Standard.

Tests: 76 new tests across src/buzz/* (event signing/verification, identity
loading, dispatch fan-out, relay-client connection lifecycle including a
real epoch-guard reconnect test against a fake WebSocket) plus fast-checker
formatter/queue coverage.

* fix(buzz): keep node engines floor at >=20

asachs01's PR raised the framework-wide engines floor to node >=22 for the
Nostr/buzz inbound relay, which relies on Node 22's native WebSocket global.
The adapter self-degrades on runtimes that predate that global, so the inbound
feature does not require raising the floor for the entire framework. Keep the
baseline at >=20 so node-20 users retain the adapter (inbound auto-disabled
below node 22).

+# Buzz (Nostr/NIP-29) Adapter — Setup
+
+This guide covers standing up an agent that can be messaged over a Buzz relay
+(NIP-29 group chat over Nostr), alongside its existing Telegram connection.
+
+## 1. Prerequisites
+
+- A running Buzz relay you control or have admin access to (see the relay's
+  own docs for standing one up — this guide assumes one already exists at
+  some `wss://relay.example.com`).
+- `buzz-admin`, the relay's operator CLI, available to whoever is
+  provisioning agent identities and channel membership.
+
+## 2. Mint the agent's Nostr identity
+
+Buzz identity minting is a deliberate, out-of-band operator step — `cortextos
+add-agent --buzz-channel` never auto-generates or prints a private key for
+you. Generate one yourself:
+
+```bash
+buzz-admin generate-key
+# prints a hex secret key + the corresponding hex pubkey
+```
+
+Keep the secret key somewhere safe; you'll put it in the agent's `.env` in
+step 4, never in `buzz.json`.
+
+## 3. Register the agent as a relay member
+
+The relay only accepts events from pubkeys it knows about (if
+`BUZZ_REQUIRE_RELAY_MEMBERSHIP` is enabled on the relay) or from pubkeys
+listed on the `pubkey_allowlist` (if `BUZZ_PUBKEY_ALLOWLIST` is enabled).
+Ask whoever administers the relay to add the agent's pubkey:
+
+```bash
+buzz-admin add-member <agent-hex-pubkey>
+# or, for an allowlist-only relay:
+# INSERT INTO pubkey_allowlist (pubkey) VALUES (decode('<agent-hex-pubkey>', 'hex'));
+```
+
+You'll also need the channel UUID(s) the agent should listen on — ask the
+channel owner, or use `cortextos buzz discover-channels` (step 6) once
+credentials are in place.
+
+## 4. Scaffold the agent
+
+```bash
+cortextos add-agent <name> --org <org> --buzz-channel <channel-uuid>
+```
+
+This writes `orgs/<org>/agents/<name>/buzz.json` with the channel
+pre-filled and `pubkey` / `allowed_pubkeys` left blank/empty
+(fail-closed — an agent with an empty `allowed_pubkeys` accepts messages
+from **no one** until you explicitly grant access).
+
+Fill in `buzz.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "pubkey": "<agent-hex-pubkey-from-step-2>",
+  "display_name": "My Agent",
+  "channels": ["<channel-uuid>"],
+  "allowed_pubkeys": ["<trusted-sender-hex-pubkey>", "..."],
+  "relay_url": "wss://relay.example.com"
+}
+```
+
+`relay_url` is optional per-agent — if every agent in an org uses the same
+relay, set `BUZZ_RELAY_URL` once in the daemon's environment instead and
+omit it here.
+
+Then add the secret key to the agent's `.env` (never committed to
+`buzz.json`):
+
+```bash
+echo 'BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY=<hex-secret-key-from-step-2>' >> orgs/<org>/agents/<name>/.env
+```
+
+## 5. Understand the connection model
+
+Buzz relays are workspace-scoped like Slack, not per-agent like Telegram: one
+WebSocket connection is shared per org, opened by the org's orchestrator
+agent at boot. Every other agent in the org still needs its own `buzz.json`
+(with its own `allowed_pubkeys`), but does not open a second connection —
+messages route through the shared connection based on channel + pubkey
+matching.
+
+A missing or misconfigured Buzz setup never blocks agent or orchestrator
+startup — connection failures are logged and retried with backoff, not
+fatal.
+
+## 6. Verify
+
+Before starting the agent, confirm credentials and connectivity:
+
+```bash
+cortextos buzz test-send --channel <channel-uuid> --text "hello from cortextOS"
+```
+
+This connects, completes the NIP-42 AUTH handshake, publishes a test event,
+and waits for the relay's OK — confirming both the private key and relay
+reachability are correct before the daemon ever starts.
+
+```bash
+cortextos buzz discover-channels --agent <name>
+```
+
+Lists the pubkey and channel UUIDs configured in that agent's `buzz.json`.
+
+Then start the agent normally:
+
+```bash
+cortextos start <name>
+```
+
+## 7. Sending and receiving
+
+Once running, channel messages the agent is subscribed to and the sender is
+allowlisted for arrive automatically via the daemon (same delivery path as
+Telegram — see the agent's `CLAUDE.md` for the exact injected format). To
+send a message manually or from a script:
+
+```bash
+cortextos buzz send --channel <channel-uuid> --text "message text" [--reply-to <event-id>]
+# or, from the bus shell scripts:
+bus/send-buzz.sh <channel-uuid> "message text"
+```
+
+## Scope of this adapter
+
+Text messages in, text messages out — mirrors the initial Telegram/Slack
+MVP scope. Not yet implemented: reactions, deletions, threading beyond a
+single reply-to tag, presence/typing indicators, media uploads, or dynamic
+channel discovery via relay-signed group-state events (channels are
+statically configured in `buzz.json` today).

+import type { NostrEvent } from './event.js';
+import { isBuzzChannelConfigured, isBuzzPubkeyAllowed, type BuzzChannelConfig } from './identity.js';
+
+/**
+ * Routes incoming Buzz (Nostr kind:9) channel-message events to every
+ * registered agent whose `buzz.json` matches BOTH gates:
+ *   1. channel match — the agent listens on the event's channel, and
+ *   2. pubkey match — the event author is in the agent's allowed_pubkeys.
+ *
+ * Buzz channels are N:1 (an agent can be a member of several channels, and
+ * a channel can have several member agents) — unlike Telegram's 1:1
+ * bot-per-agent shape, a single relay connection fans an incoming message
+ * out to every matching agent, not just the first.
+ */
+
+export interface BuzzDispatchTarget {
+  agentName: string;
+  config: BuzzChannelConfig;
+}
+
+export interface BuzzDispatchResult {
+  agentName: string;
+  event: NostrEvent;
+  channelId: string;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Registry of agents this daemon knows to be listening on Buzz. The relay
+ * client's onMessage handler feeds events through `dispatch()`.
+ */
+export class BuzzDispatcher {
+  private targets: Map<string, BuzzDispatchTarget> = new Map();
+
+  /** Registers or updates an agent's Buzz config. */
+  register(agentName: string, config: BuzzChannelConfig): void {
+    this.targets.set(agentName, { agentName, config });
+  }
+
+  /** Removes an agent from dispatch (e.g. on stopAgent). */
+  unregister(agentName: string): void {
+    this.targets.delete(agentName);
+  }
+
+  /**
+   * Computes every agent that should receive this event: channel match AND
+   * pubkey-allowed match. Delivers to all matches, not just the first.
+   */
+  dispatch(channelId: string, event: NostrEvent): BuzzDispatchResult[] {
+    const results: BuzzDispatchResult[] = [];
+    for (const target of this.targets.values()) {
+      if (!isBuzzChannelConfigured(target.config, channelId)) continue;
+      if (!isBuzzPubkeyAllowed(target.config, event.pubkey)) continue;
+      results.push({ agentName: target.agentName, event, channelId });
+    }
+    return results;
+  }
+
+  /** Union of every channel id across all registered agents — what the relay client should subscribe to. */
+  allChannels(): string[] {
+    const channels = new Set<string>();
+    for (const target of this.targets.values()) {
+      for (const c of target.config.channels) channels.add(c);
+    }
+    return [...channels];
+  }
+}

+import { sha256 } from '@noble/hashes/sha2.js';
+import { hmac } from '@noble/hashes/hmac.js';
+import { schnorr, utils as secpUtils, hashes as secpHashes } from '@noble/secp256k1';
+import { bytesToHex, hexToBytes, utf8ToBytes, concatBytes } from '@noble/hashes/utils.js';
+
+// @noble/secp256k1 v3 requires the consumer to wire in its hash functions
+// rather than bundling one itself (keeps the core package hash-agnostic).
+// Without this, schnorr.sign/verify throw "hashes.sha256 not set" at
+// runtime — set once at module load, before any signing/verification call.
+secpHashes.sha256 = sha256;
+secpHashes.hmacSha256 = (key: Uint8Array, ...messages: Uint8Array[]) =>
+  hmac(sha256, key, concatBytes(...messages));
+
+/**
+ * Minimal Nostr (NIP-01) event construction and signing — the narrow subset
+ * Buzz's NIP-29 direct-connection protocol needs: build the canonical
+ * serialization, hash it to get the event id, and produce a BIP-340 schnorr
+ * signature over that id.
+ *
+ * Deliberately not a general-purpose Nostr SDK: no relay-list parsing, no
+ * NIP-04/44 encryption, no bech32 (npub/nsec) helpers. Buzz agents only need
+ * to sign and publish kind:9 (channel message) and kind:22242 (NIP-42 auth)
+ * events, and optionally verify relay-signed discovery events.
+ *
+ * Uses `@noble/secp256k1` + `@noble/hashes` for the schnorr signature and
+ * sha256 hashing rather than a hand-rolled implementation — see the "New
+ * dependency" note in docs/superpowers/specs/sp4-buzz-adapter-design.md and
+ * the PR description for why this one exception to the zero-deps convention
+ * was made.
+ */
+
+export interface NostrTag extends Array<string> {}
+
+export interface UnsignedNostrEvent {
+  pubkey: string;
+  created_at: number;
+  kind: number;
+  tags: NostrTag[];
+  content: string;
+}
+
+export interface NostrEvent extends UnsignedNostrEvent {
+  id: string;
+  sig: string;
+}
+
+/**
+ * Computes the NIP-01 event id: sha256 of the canonical JSON serialization
+ * `[0, pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content]` with no extra whitespace.
+ */
+export function computeEventId(event: UnsignedNostrEvent): string {
+  const serialized = JSON.stringify([
+    0,
+    event.pubkey,
+    event.created_at,
+    event.kind,
+    event.tags,
+    event.content,
+  ]);
+  return bytesToHex(sha256(utf8ToBytes(serialized)));
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds and signs a Nostr event.
+ *
+ * @param kind Nostr event kind (9 = channel message, 22242 = NIP-42 auth).
+ * @param content Event content (message text; empty string for AUTH events).
+ * @param tags Event tags (e.g. `[["h", channelId]]`).
+ * @param secretKeyHex Hex-encoded 32-byte secp256k1 secret key.
+ */
+export function buildEvent(
+  kind: number,
+  content: string,
+  tags: NostrTag[],
+  secretKeyHex: string,
+): NostrEvent {
+  const secretKey = hexToBytes(secretKeyHex);
+  const pubkey = bytesToHex(schnorr.getPublicKey(secretKey));
+
+  const unsigned: UnsignedNostrEvent = {
+    pubkey,
+    created_at: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
+    kind,
+    tags,
+    content,
+  };
+
+  const id = computeEventId(unsigned);
+  const sig = bytesToHex(schnorr.sign(hexToBytes(id), secretKey));
+
+  return { ...unsigned, id, sig };
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds a NIP-42 kind:22242 AUTH event responding to a relay challenge.
+ * Tags: `[["relay", relayUrl], ["challenge", challenge]]`, per the wire
+ * protocol in NOSTR.md / buzz-ws-client's connection.rs reference.
+ */
+export function buildAuthEvent(
+  challenge: string,
+  relayUrl: string,
+  secretKeyHex: string,
+): NostrEvent {
+  return buildEvent(22242, '', [
+    ['relay', relayUrl],
+    ['challenge', challenge],
+  ], secretKeyHex);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Builds a kind:9 channel message event. `replyToEventId`, when provided,
+ * adds a NIP-10 `["e", "<parent-event-id>", "", "reply"]` tag.
+ */
+export function buildChannelMessageEvent(
+  channelId: string,
+  content: string,
+  secretKeyHex: string,
+  replyToEventId?: string,
+): NostrEvent {
+  const tags: NostrTag[] = [['h', channelId]];
+  if (replyToEventId) {
+    tags.push(['e', replyToEventId, '', 'reply']);
+  }
+  return buildEvent(9, content, tags, secretKeyHex);
+}
+
+/**
+ * Verifies a (typically relay-signed) event's signature and id integrity.
+ * Returns false on any malformed input rather than throwing — callers treat
+ * an unverifiable event as untrusted, not as an error condition.
+ */
+export function verifyEvent(event: NostrEvent): boolean {
+  try {
+    const unsigned: UnsignedNostrEvent = {
+      pubkey: event.pubkey,
+      created_at: event.created_at,
+      kind: event.kind,
+      tags: event.tags,
+      content: event.content,
+    };
+    const expectedId = computeEventId(unsigned);
+    if (expectedId !== event.id) return false;
+    return schnorr.verify(hexToBytes(event.sig), hexToBytes(event.id), hexToBytes(event.pubkey));
+  } catch {
+    return false;
+

commits.subject: fix(opencode): auto-recover exit-0 --continue wedge and confirm-dead stale reap (#927)
commits.body:
An opencode agent whose --continue session is wedged exits with code 0 on the
bootstrap splash; crash-recovery re-runs --continue, re-attaches the same wedged
session, and re-exits 0 — a self-perpetuating loop that drains max_crashes and
HALTs the agent (measured live 2026-08-12: 10 exit_code=0 crashes in 22min).

Fix A (drop-continue-on-wedge): after THRESHOLD (3) consecutive fast exit_code=0
exits in continue mode, arm .force-fresh so the next boot discards the wedged
session. Like image-poison recovery, the restart is not charged against
max_crashes_per_day (a continuity artifact, not a malfunction).

Fix B (confirm-dead reap): stale-process cleanup now escalates SIGTERM -> poll ->
SIGKILL and confirms the process is dead before unlinking the marker, instead of
fire-and-forget SIGTERM.

Does NOT include the enabled+unmapped+stale-heartbeat liveness detector for the
silent-dormancy failure mode; that is tracked separately and is required before
this class is fully closed.

Caveat: the wedge threshold assumes the default crash-window max. An agent
configured with a tight custom crash_window (max_crashes < 3) may HALT via the
crash-loop pauser before the force-fresh recovery fires.

commits.subject: fix(daemon): reload crons.json on tick when its mtime advances (#928)
commits.body:
CronScheduler.tick() fired the in-memory schedule but never re-read
crons.json, so a durable edit (prompt or schedule) only took effect on an
explicit IPC reload signal or a daemon restart. The best-effort IPC
signal in signalCronReload() swallows send errors, and its comment
falsely claimed the scheduler would pick up the change on the next tick.

tick() now stats crons.json and calls the existing reload() when the
file's mtime has advanced since the last load, so a durable edit applies
within one tick with no restart. The tracked mtime is refreshed only in
loadCrons(), never after tick's own bookkeeping writes, so a post-fire
write cannot mask an external edit that landed while a fire was awaiting.

Also reorders the reload-while-firing guard ahead of the changeKey
preservation branch (a latent orphaned-entry bug the new reload path
would otherwise expose) and corrects the two false comments in bus.ts.

Adds unit and real-file integration coverage, including a positive-control
test for the do-not-refresh-after-own-writes property.

Co-authored-by: Boris <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(telegram): exponential backoff with jitter on poller transient errors (#922)
commits.body:
The poll loop retried every transient getUpdates error (timeout, 429, 5xx)
after a fixed 1s interval, hammering the API on persistent failures and
ignoring Telegram's 429 retry_after hint. Add exponential backoff with
additive jitter, honor retry_after (bounded by a 5-minute ceiling so an
absurd value cannot freeze the poller), cap the exponential curve at 30s,
and reset on a successful poll. The 409 Conflict self-die and
intentional-stop paths are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Boris <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: James Goldbach
commits.subject: fix(daemon): make startAgent idempotent for duplicate starts on a live agent (#923)
commits.body:
A duplicate startAgent against a healthy agent queued a pendingRestarts
entry and logged a spurious BUG-011 REGRESSION CHECK warning, causing a
later spurious restart. Add a stoppingAgents marker claimed synchronously
at stopAgent entry so the alive-branch distinguishes a legit in-flight
restart (queue) from a pure duplicate start (idempotent no-op). Soften the
now-stale BUG-011 warnings on the expected legit-restart path to info, and
document the stop-before-start ordering invariant.

Co-authored-by: Boris <noreply@anthropic.com>
